title: EFC Phase 3: SPARC Validation
description: Unbinned maximum-likelihood fit with intrinsic scatter of the EFC screening form ln μ = k ln(1 + g†/gbar) to 174 SPARC galaxies (3264 points). The analysis finds k = 0.415 ± 0.029, g† = (2.51 ± 0.60) × 10^-10 m/s^2, and σ_int ≈ 0.14 dex, and—using an independently obtained aG = 0.094 ± 0.01—infers a cross-scale phase-gain parameter C = 4.4 ± 0.6. This establishes empirical compatibility of EFC with the RAR and provides a quantitative cross-scale consistency check.

screening_form_mu.description: EFC screening form for the gravitational enhancement factor relating observed to baryonic acceleration.

log_screening.description: Log-linear form used for unbinned maximum-likelihood fitting of the RAR.

likelihood_with_scatter.description: Unbinned maximum-likelihood with intrinsic scatter for y_i = ln(g_obs,i / g_bar,i).

geff_expansion.description: Core Lock relation linking effective gravity to entropy-phase accumulation with universal coupling a_G.

phase_gain_relation.description: EFC phase accumulation ansatz connecting galactic and cosmological scales; k factors into a universal coupling a_G and a phase-gain parameter C.

key_results.main_finding: EFC’s screening form provides an excellent empirical fit to the SPARC RAR with k = 0.415 ± 0.029, g† = (2.51 ± 0.60) × 10^-10 m/s^2, and σ_int ≈ 0.14 dex, and—combined with aG = 0.094 ± 0.01—implies a cross-scale phase-gain C = 4.4 ± 0.6.
datasets_used: SPARC (Lelli et al. 2016): 174 galaxies, 3264 points, quality Q ≤ 2, inclination > 30°

kill_criteria: KC1: In an expanded SPARC-quality sample (>= 300 galaxies) analyzed with the same unbinned MLE and intrinsic-scatter framework, the EFC screening form ln μ = k ln(1 + g†/gbar) exhibits a statistically significant residual trend with gbar (nonzero residual slope) at >5σ, indicating the functional form is incompatible with the RAR.
KC2: The asymptotic low-acceleration slope measured from stacked or binned RAR data is inconsistent with the EFC prediction d(ln μ)/d(ln gbar) = −k by >5σ when k is obtained from the global fit.

KC3: Independent H0-scale analyses converge on a universal coupling a_G that is inconsistent with 0.094 ± 0.01 by >5σ and lead to mutually incompatible values of C = k/a_G between the RAR fit and H0-inferred a_G (no single C fits both within 3σ), breaking EFC’s cross-scale consistency.

KC4: Across multiple high-quality rotation-curve datasets, model selection decisively favors an alternative parametric form (e.g., ΔAIC > 20) that cannot be recast as ln μ ∝ ln(1 + g†/gbar) with a single global k and g†.

KC5: The inferred transition scale g† is found to correlate strongly with galaxy properties (e.g., central surface density) with |ρ| > 0.7, contradicting the assumption of a single global acceleration scale in the EFC screening ansatz.

related_packages.role: Independent source of a_G used to derive C

subtitle: Empirical Test of Energy-Flow Cosmology Against the Radial Acceleration Relation

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes that EFC’s screening ansatz ln μ = k ln(1 + g†/gbar) provides an excellent, low-scatter empirical description of the SPARC RAR and yields a concrete cross-scale link C = k/a_G when combined with an independently measured a_G from the H0 regime. It anchors EFC’s galaxy-scale phenomenology with calibrated parameters (k, g†, σ_int) and sets up falsifiable RAR-specific kill criteria for future, larger samples and cross-dataset model selection. It does not resolve theory gaps but strengthens the empirical bridge between galaxy dynamics and cosmological coupling.
graph_insights: Introduces the first direct EFC linkage to SPARC/RAR and rotation curves in the graph, connecting EFC’s screening function node to empirical galaxy dynamics.
Defines new parameter nodes (k, g†, C) with edges to both galaxy-scale (SPARC) and cosmological-scale (a_G from H0) observables, tightening cross-domain constraints.

page_updates.new_text: An unbinned MLE fit with intrinsic scatter of the EFC screening form ln μ = k ln(1 + g†/gbar) to SPARC (174 galaxies; 3264 points) yields k = 0.415 ± 0.029, g† = (2.51 ± 0.60) × 10^-10 m s^-2, and σ_int ≈ 0.14 dex. Combining with an independently inferred a_G = 0.094 ± 0.01 (H0-regime) implies a cross-scale phase-gain C = 4.4 ± 0.6, establishing empirical cross-scale compatibility within the EFC projection framework.
page_updates.reasoning: The paper provides new calibrated parameters and a cross-scale link that belong in the formal exposition of EFC’s galaxy-scale phenomenology.

page_updates.new_text: Phase 3 SPARC validation completed: EFC screening ansatz fits the SPARC RAR with low intrinsic scatter and yields a cross-scale C consistent with the independently measured a_G from H0-scale analyses.
page_updates.reasoning: This is a concrete milestone demonstrating galaxy-scale empirical compatibility and cross-scale consistency.

implicit_consequences: The measured k implies a low-acceleration RAR slope d(ln μ)/d(ln gbar) = −0.415 ± 0.029, defining a clear target for independent slope extractions (stacked/binned) to test KC2-style failures.
The inferred global g† distinct from MOND’s a0 provides a discriminant in model selection across high-quality rotation-curve datasets.
C = 4.4 ± 0.6 now serves as a cross-scale anchor; future updates to a_G or galaxy-scale fits must maintain a single consistent C to avoid KC3-type cross-scale inconsistency.

The achieved σ_int ≈ 0.14 dex indicates EFC’s screening form does not inflate RAR scatter, supporting viability for broader samples and enabling KC5-style correlation checks of g† against galaxy properties.
